'''''Fascicularia''''' is a monotypic [[genus]] of [[flowering plant]]s in the pineapple [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Bromeliaceae]], subfamily [[Bromelioideae]]. The genus name is from the Latin ''fasciculus'' (bundle) and ''arius'' (pertaining to).<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.bsi.org/brom_info/genera.html |title=Bromeliad Info - Genera Etymology |access-date=2009-10-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070203011214/http://www.bsi.org/brom_info/genera.html |archive-date=2007-02-03 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Only one species is known, '''''Fascicularia bicolor'''''. It is endemic to [[Chile]]<ref name=nnn>[http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=245006 Kew World Checklist of Selected Plant Families]</ref> and reportedly naturalized in [[France]] and the extreme south and west of [[Great Britain]].<ref name=BSBI>{{cite web |work=BSBI Maps |title=Fascicularia distribution map |url=https://bsbi.org/maps?taxonid=2cd4p9h.3hkxg0 |access-date=18 August 2020 }}</ref> In the wild, all ''Fascicularias'' are [[wiktionary:saxicolous|saxicolous]] (growing on rocks) or [[epiphyte]]s.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Zizka |first1=G |last2=Horres |first2=R |last3=Nelson |first3=C |last4=Weising |first4=K |date=1999 |title=Revision of the genus Fascicularia Mez (Bromeliaceae) |url=https://academic.oup.com/botlinnean/article/129/4/315/2557320 |journal=Botanical Journal of the Linnean Society |volume=129 |issue=4 |pages=315–332 |doi=10.1111/j.1095-8339.1999.tb00507.x |access-date=30 May 2022|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Ortega-Solis |first1=G |last2=Díaz |first2=I |last3=Mellado-Mansilla |first3=D |last4=Moreno-González |first4=R |last5=Godoy |first5=J |last6=Samaniego |first6=H |date=2020 |title=The importance of tree species and size for the epiphytic bromeliad Fascicularia bicolor in a South-American temperate rainforest (Chile) |url=http://www.sisef.it/iforest/contents/?id=ifor2710-013 |journal=IForest - Biogeosciences and Forestry |volume=13 |issue=2 |pages=92–97 |doi= 10.3832/ifor2710-013 |s2cid=214699975 |access-date=30 May 2022|url-access=subscription |doi-access=free }}</ref>

It is cultivated in gardens for the dramatic bright crimson colour of its leaves contrasting with the blue inflorescence.<ref name=RHS>{{cite web|title=''Fascicularia bicolor'', Crimson bromeliad |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/7145/Fascicularia-bicolor/Details |publisher=Royal Horticultural Society |access-date=18 August 2020}}</ref>

The edible fruits are similar to those of the species ''[[Greigia sphacelata]]'', but smaller; They are consumed in the same way as these.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Pfanzelt |first1=Simon |last2=García |first2=Carolina|last3=Marticorena |first3=Alicia |date=2013 |title=Notes on the Chilean geographic distribution of several vascular plant species |url=https://public.pensoft.net/items/?p=7TVeXpoqfNYT89tyrm3ifrTeG9Wv8P676JSQp%2FH2pj9hhtoybol4GF7LEbj3fxHT5Fo8esHsttgAZJlgYxTDbAHCHfwWCPk5a45KhiTLFAvASBIF%2FwVyLbjF5HKmbQ%3D%3D&n=gTJLSd4CdNEGg8l0u3Docbj1T4Dr7LmW4p7g5qjy7Sk%3D |journal=Check List |volume=9 |issue=4 |pages=832–837 |doi=10.15560/9.4.832 |doi-access=free |access-date=4 June 2023}}</ref>

==Subspecies==
Two subspecies are recognized:
* ''Fascicularia bicolor'' subsp. ''bicolor''
* ''Fascicularia bicolor'' subsp. ''canaliculata'' <small>E.C.Nelson & Zizka</small>
